text:
maria: Seeing a perf regression in prod on ROCm clusters. Starts at ~seqlen 513. Kernels missing for sparse-attn path so requests fall back to generic matmul and latency spikes. Noted ~3x latency for 1024 tokens.

kevin: ugh. which kernel signatures are missing? is this the new sparse kernel we rolled last week?

maria: Looks like the signed kernels for arch gfx1030+ with seqlen>=512 aren't being picked. Profiler shows kernel_lookup returned NOT_FOUND for `sparse_attn_qual_gfx1030_seqlen_>=512`.

sanjay: can you paste the profiler snippet? also which runtime version?

maria: runtime v2.8.1-prod. profiler dump:

```
# kernel lookup trace
model=redwood-tiny, op=attention_forward, arch=gfx1030, seqlen=1024
candidate_kernels: [sparse_attn_gfx1030_512_optimized, sparse_attn_gfx1030_256, matmul_generic]
lookup_result: NOT_FOUND -> fallback: matmul_generic
exec_time_matmul: 32ms/token (observed)
```

kevin: That `sparse_attn_gfx1030_512_optimized` should have been published in the last autotune batch. Did the autotuner skip gfx1030 due to failing CI?

build-bot: CI: autotune-gfx1030 job failed on pytest::test_kernel_smoke - OOM on small alloc. Job id: 4392.

maria: yep build-bot confirms. The autotune artifact wasn't promoted. But we still expect a soft-route to `sparse_attn_gfx1030_256` for longer sequences (with segmented execution). Instead the kernel selector rejects it because of a strict match on seqlen binning.

taylor: That sounds like our sequence-length binning is too aggressive. We used an exact-match policy for 512/1024 to avoid micro-inefficiencies, but with missing artifacts we should fall back to a compatible kernel instead of matmul.

sanjay: Agreed. Minimal short-term mitigation: update kernel selector policy to allow "compatible" matches when artifact_count < threshold. I can push a hotfix to runtime routing rules to relax seqlen matching for ROCm only. Thoughts?

kevin: +1 for ROCm-only change. But add a canary so we can verify no correctness regressions. Also log when compatibility route is used so we can measure perf delta.

maria: For telemetry, please add a tag `kernel_route=compatible_fallback` and include which kernel it chose. We saw memory differences when using `_256` on 1024 sequences (KV segmentation), need to ensure KV cache correctness.

sanjay: Will do. Also planning: re-run autotune on gfx1030 with smaller memory settings to avoid OOMs. That should produce the missing artifacts and allow us to reintroduce strict binning.

kevin: Can we apply a temporary batching heuristic tweak too? If we detect sequences >512 on ROCm, prefer smaller batch sizes to avoid memory pressure. That's cheaper than dropping to matmul.

taylor: Good idea. I'll add a policy: if arch contains `gfx` and seqlen > 512 then reduce batch target by 30% and enable KV-segmentation toggles. We'll canary on 5% of traffic.

maria: I'm worried about correctness around KV segmentation + compatible kernel. Add an internal check in the runtime: after a compatible kernel path runs, validate first 8 tokens against reference (fast checksum) in debug builds. Only enable on canary traffic.

kevin: +1. Also create an alert if tail-latency increases >50% post-change.

ops-bot: deploy request: staging routing-policy update -> canary 5% (sanjay). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3542

maria: I'll run a focused perf job: compare `matmul_generic` vs `sparse_attn_gfx1030_256` on seqlen 1024 with batch=1 and batch=4, capture KV hit/miss counts.

build-bot: perf job queued: perf-gfx1030-1024-202. Job id: 5591.

kevin: For the longer-term fix: autotune should mark artifacts as "partial" if some checks OOM but others pass, and the selector should be able to use partial artifacts with a deprecation window. Avoids full rollback.

sanjay: noted. I'll write a spec for partial-artifact promotion and a route-cost penalty for partials. Estimated 2 sprints.

maria: tl;dr action items: (1) sanjay hotfix to relax seqlen matching on ROCm (canary 5%), (2) taylor batching tweak canary 5%, (3) telemetry tag + KV checksum on canary, (4) rerun autotune with adjusted memory settings, (5) spec for partial-artifact promotion.

kevin: sounds good. keep updates here. thanks.
